ri-sl-openstates-roster.title: Sitting Rhode Island legislators and general officers
ri-sl-openstates-roster.note: Who holds each seat today, and which candidate is the seat's sitting member (same chamber and district, or the same office; the name fits; one fit only). A candidate for another seat is tied to a sitting member (not marked incumbent) only when the name fits exactly one sitting legislator or general officer, of the same party. The roster's general officers are the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State and Attorney General only; for the General Treasurer the holder is left empty. Names, party and ids only; the roster's contact columns are never selected.

ri-sl-census-2024-counties.note: Five-digit county codes (GEOID) for Rhode Island's five counties.

ri-sl-census-2024-towns.title: Cartographic boundary file, county subdivisions, Rhode Island, 2024 (1:500,000)
ri-sl-census-2024-towns.note: Rhode Island's 39 cities and towns and the county each lies in, matched by name to the results' town rows (every one matched). The counties a district reaches are those of the towns its September 9 primary contests were counted in (derived).

ri-sl-boe-2026-primary-results.title: 2026 Statewide Primary (September 9, 2026): official results, state offices
ri-sl-boe-2026-primary-results.note: From the Board's election results site's data service (marked isOfficialResults), statewide and town by town, the same service the federal loader reads; linked from https://elections.ri.gov/elections/previous-election-results. 142 state contests read (general officers, Senate, House), kept as figures only in ri_2026_primary_state.json; every candidate checked (175): the towns add up to the statewide figure, the count groups add up and equal the summary report's, and each contest's total equals the sum of its candidates. No write-in votes are reported for these contests. The asterisk the results print after the party-endorsed candidate's name is taken off and said in the note. A field is a party primary with two candidates or more; a party's only candidate is its nominee without a contest and is named in the race's note. Not read here: 6 Congress contests (the federal loader's), 19 party committee contests (party offices, not on the November ballot) and 25 city and town contests (local).

ri-sl-boe-2026-primary-summary.title: Summary Results Report, OFFICIAL RESULTS, Primary Election 2026, September 9, 2026 (Prim26_Summary.pdf)
ri-sl-boe-2026-primary-summary.note: Control: each state candidate's TOTAL, Election Day, Early Voting and Mail Ballots votes equal the results service's; Total Votes Cast equals the sum of the candidates; each statewide contest's Contest Totals, plus the party's federal-only mail ballots (the votes in the results' Federal unit of its Senator in Congress contest, a unit only the Congress contests carry: DEMOCRAT 191, REPUBLICAN 1), equals the report's Ballots Cast for the party (DEMOCRAT 134,220, REPUBLICAN 24,204), the difference falling wholly in Mail Ballots.
